issues.claim: Principle 1.2 of the ACM Code of Ethics ("Avoid harm") requires those who caused unintended harm to undo or mitigate it as much as possible
issues.problem: The ACM link returned 403 and has no excerpt, so the wording cannot be confirmed from the item. From memory the 2018 Code does say this in 1.2 ("When that harm is unintended, those responsible are obliged to undo or mitigate the harm as much as possible"), but that is not evidence.
issues.suggestedFix: Re-fetch the ACM page via an accessible mirror, or quote the sentence in the notes. Keep the claim only if the wording is confirmed.

issues.claim: Principle 1.7 on confidentiality also does not oblige you to keep secret what is evidence of a violation of law, organisational regulations or the Code itself.
issues.problem: Not verifiable from the item because the ACM page was not fetched. I recall 1.7 containing this exception in the 2018 Code. Applying it here is also a stretch: the teammate's request is not a confidentiality obligation about client data, and corrupted balances are not clearly a violation of law or regulation.
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm the 1.7 wording from the fetched page. Then soften it, e.g. "Principle 1.7 also makes confidentiality yield where the information is evidence of a violation of law, organisational regulations or the Code, and in any case a private promise between colleagues is not a confidentiality duty to protect." Alternatively drop the 1.7 sentence.
